steps: Perform finish milling on a lathed part using a horizontal milling machine at a milling speed of 1200 RPM with a climb milling tool path that follows the contour, achieving a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, taking 63 minutes to complete, after which the resulting milled part is placed on a conveyor belt.

On a CNC Turning Center, a precision turning operation is performed on a lathed part loaded from a conveyor belt, using CNC program TC-842 with spindle speed set to 850 RPM and tool offsets verified and calibrated for all 6 tools, taking 84 minutes to produce a finished machined component that is then transferred to a mobile robot.

Using a punch press, a sheet metal component on a conveyor belt undergoes a punching operation with a 12 mm circular punch at a stroke speed of 120 strokes per minute and laser-aligned die alignment within ±0.05 mm tolerance, lasting for 3 minutes, to produce a finished sheet metal product that is then transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Gear Shaper machine, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with 32 teeth through a gear shaping operation running at 180 strokes per minute for 53 minutes, resulting in a shaped gear that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

Using a drill press, a metal bar is drilled with an 8 mm twist drill at a spindle speed of 950 RPM and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev for 1 minute, resulting in a drilled component that is transferred to a mobile robot.

A ground part is precision cut using wire EDM cutting on a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) with a 0.25 mm brass wire, operating at a peak current of 6 A and a pulse duration of 10 µs, achieving a cutting speed of 8 mm/min, and the operation runs for 35 minutes, resulting in a precision finished part transferred to a conveyor belt.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs precision milling on a milled part loaded from a conveyor belt, using a 5-axis simultaneous diamond-coated end mill with an active damping system engaged to maintain a milling precision of ±0.005 mm, completing the operation in 20 minutes, and resulting in a ground part transferred to a mobile robot.

On the Gear Shaper, a broached component is shaped into a helical gear with 24 teeth through a gear shaping operation running at 160 strokes per minute for 43 minutes, resulting in a shaped gear placed on a conveyor belt.

The milled part is surface planed on a planer for 85 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 2.0 mm per pass and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/stroke to produce a planed part with a surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm, which is then transferred to a conveyor belt.

Using a drill press, a metal bar is drilled with a 10 mm carbide drill at a spindle speed of 750 RPM and a feed rate of 0.18 mm/rev for 21 minutes, resulting in a drilled component that is then placed on a conveyor belt.

The bandsaw performs a cutting to length operation on a metal bar loaded from a conveyor belt, running for 10 minutes at a saw speed of 60 m/min using a bi-metal variable tooth blade with a cutting width of 3.2 mm kerf, resulting in a lathed part transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a broached component to create an involute gear profile with a 20° pressure angle, running at a hobbing speed of 220 RPM and a feed rate of 1.5 mm/rev, lasting for 77 minutes, resulting in a hobbied gear that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a Hobbing Machine, gear hobbing is performed on a broached component for 18 minutes, using a hobbing speed of 260 RPM and a feed rate of 1.2 mm/rev to produce an involute gear profile with a 14.5° pressure angle, resulting in a hobbied gear that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.
